common.sameAsFo: Same voice as the First Officer
common.noListPressRefresh: No voice list yet. Press Refresh voices.
common.pressNow: Press the key or button now…
common.lampTitle: Lights while the bound input is held

general.title: Voice First Officer
general.hint: Voices are tried in order: Kokoro, ElevenLabs, Google, then Windows

localOnly.label: Local only
localOnly.hint: Never use network voices. Speech never leaves this PC.
localOnly.more: Kokoro, ElevenLabs and Google are skipped on every path.

seat.label: Your seat
seat.hint: The seat you fly from. The First Officer works the other side.
seat.more: Left: the FO uses the right MCDU, EFIS and controls. Right: the FO uses the captain's side. The MCDU side changes after an app restart.

engineFlap.label: Engine & flap call responses
engineFlap.hint: The FO answers your engine start, flap and anti-ice calls.
engineFlap.more: Flap calls are checked against the placard speeds. Verbal only: the FO never moves the levers.

engineStart.label: Engine start monitoring
engineStart.hint: The FO calls each engine start: starting, available, both stabilized.
engineStart.more: Read from the engine data on the ground, once per start. No pilot call needed.

readThrough.label: Read through lines already set
readThrough.hint: A checklist line whose switch is already correct is spoken with its answer and completed. No reply needed.
readThrough.more: The FO says the line and the answer in one breath, e.g. "Flaps, retracted." Lines that need a read-back (numbers, flap config), lines with no live value from ProSim, and lines without a dataref still wait for your reply. Off: every line waits for you.

answerCourtesies.label: Answer thank you
answerCourtesies.hint: The FO says “You’re welcome, Captain” when you thank it right after it did something.
answerCourtesies.more: Only within 20 seconds of the FO’s last word or action, never on the takeoff roll, in the initial climb or on the rollout, and never for a low-confidence transcript. Whisper writes “Thank you.” for a breath — that is why this is off by default.

pacing.title: Human Pacing
pacing.hint: Button presses at a human tempo

humanize.label: Humanize button timing
humanize.hint: Add small human pauses between button presses.

tempo.label: Tempo
tempo.hint: 1.0 is normal, 2.0 is twice as slow.

outputDevice.label: Output device
outputDevice.hint: Where the First Officer's voice plays.

intercomFilter.label: Intercom filter
intercomFilter.hint: Make the FO sound like a headset, not a narrator.

persona.title: FO Persona
persona.hint: Wording and tone only. A number, a callout or a checklist line is never changed

enabled.hint: Let the persona colour what the FO says.
enabled.more: With the language model off, the only effect is varied acknowledgements.

name.label: Name
name.hint: Woven into the model's style prompt ("Your name is …"). Empty = unnamed.

formality.label: Formality
formality.hint: How formal the FO is with you.

chattiness.label: Chattiness
chattiness.hint: 0 keeps everything short. 3 allows natural warmth.
chattiness.more: "Quiet please" silences chatter for the session whatever this says.

styles.title: What the Persona Styles
styles.hint: Each one is verified against the facts; the plain text is always the fallback

advisories.label: Advisories
advisories.hint: Flow and weather advisories pass through the model before they are spoken.
advisories.more: Only when the restyle returns within the time below; otherwise the plain text speaks.

vary.label: Vary acknowledgements
vary.hint: Pick "are you sure" / "say again" lines at random from phrases.json instead of in turn.

budget.label: Advisory restyle budget
budget.hint: Time the model gets to restyle one advisory. The plain text speaks when it runs out.

styles.poolsBefore: The phrase pools themselves are in
styles.poolsAfter: — edit the file, the FO reloads it.

listening.title: Recognition & Push-to-Talk
listening.hint: How the First Officer hears you

mode.label: Listening mode
mode.hint: Push-to-talk: the FO listens only while your FO key is held.
mode.more: Continuous: the FO listens whenever it expects a reply, except while the ATC key is held. On a network (VATSIM, IVAO, SayIntentions) always bind your ATC transmit key below, so the FO never hears what you say to ATC.

foPtt.label: FO push-to-talk
foPtt.hint: The key or button that talks to the First Officer. Never your ATC key.

atcPtt.label: ATC push-to-talk (mute)
atcPtt.hint: The key or button you use to talk to ATC. While it is held, the FO does not listen.

atcMuteSource.label: ATC mute from a ProSim switch
atcMuteSource.hint: A sidestick or hand-mic PTT switch in ProSim. While it reads pushed, the FO does not listen — same as the key or button above, and it needs no joystick on this PC.
atcMuteSource.more: Bind your button to the switch in ProSim (it can live on another PC). Choosing a SayIntentions push-to-talk switch on the SayIntentions section sets this to the same switch when it is still Off.

joystickButtons.label: Also listen for joystick buttons
joystickButtons.hint: Off: Set captures a keyboard key only. On: Set also watches the joystick buttons on this PC.
joystickButtons.more: Windows' joystick layer has crashed the app on some PCs (2026-09-20, 2026-10-10, 2026-10-11 — the last time just from listing the devices when this page opened). The page now talks to it only while this is on or when you press Scan. A ProSim switch (above, and on the SayIntentions section) needs no joystick on this PC.

listening.setHint: Set waits ten seconds for a key (and a joystick button when ticked above). Save afterwards; the lamps light for the saved bindings only.

inputDevice.label: Input device
inputDevice.hint: The microphone the FO listens on.

trackUnmatched.label: Track phrases the FO did not understand
trackUnmatched.hint: Keep what you said that nothing acted on, so you can add the commands you actually use.
trackUnmatched.more: Listed under Heard but not understood on the Voice status page and written to the session log as voice.unmatched. Off: nothing is kept; the log's ASR trail still shows every utterance.

matchScore.label: Phrase match score
matchScore.hint: How close a heard phrase must be to a known one before the FO acts on it.
matchScore.more: 0.5 Levenshtein + 0.5 DoubleMetaphone. Lower hears more, mis-hears more.

confirmBelow.label: Ask 'did you mean' below
confirmBelow.hint: A match between the score above and this one makes the FO ask 'Did you mean …?' instead of acting.
confirmBelow.more: Set it equal to the match score to never ask.

noConfirmBelow.label: No 'did you mean' below
noConfirmBelow.hint: Airborne below this radio height the FO never asks 'Did you mean …?'. The takeoff roll, initial climb and landing rollout are always quiet.
noConfirmBelow.more: In those moments an FMA read or capture call that matched at 0.70 or better is simply acknowledged ('Checked.'), and anything else is let go without a word — a question over the roll or 'did you mean gear up?' in the climb is the worst chatter there is. 0 = only the three phases.

offlineConfidence.label: Offline engine confidence
offlineConfidence.hint: Minimum confidence the Windows engine must report. Not used with a LAN server.

server.title: Speech Recognition Server
server.hint: A transcription server on your network. Empty uses the offline Windows engine

flavour.label: LAN ASR server flavour
flavour.hint: Must match the server type running at that address.
flavour.more: The wrong type answers 404 to everything while the health check stays green. A warning is logged when that happens.

vad.label: Voice activity detection
vad.hint: How the FO decides you are speaking.
vad.more: Silero ignores engine noise and the FO's own voice and hears quiet commands. RMS is the older energy gate and the fallback if the Silero model cannot load. Applies from the next listening start. Further knobs (vadMinSpeechMs, vadPreRollMs, vadMaxUtteranceMs) are file-only in settings.json.

muteMic.label: Ignore the microphone while the FO speaks
muteMic.hint: On: the FO cannot hear its own voice from the cockpit speakers and answer itself. Off only if you must talk over the FO.
muteMic.more: Also drops a transcript that repeats what the FO just said, whatever the timing. On 2026-10-10 a VBAN loop put the FO on the speakers and it chatted with itself for minutes.

micTail.label: Microphone tail after the FO speaks
micTail.hint: How long the microphone stays ignored after the FO's last word. Raise it for a loud, echoey cockpit; lower it if your quick replies are missed.

ownWords.label: Own-words window
ownWords.hint: How long after the FO said something a transcript repeating it is taken for the FO's own voice and dropped. Lower it if your replies that echo the FO's words are lost; raise it for a long speaker delay.
ownWords.more: Your answer to a 'did you mean …?' and the open checklist line's expected reply are never dropped, whatever the window.

vadThreshold.label: VAD threshold
vadThreshold.hint: Raise it if noise triggers the FO. Lower it if quiet commands are missed.

endSilence.label: End-of-utterance silence
endSilence.hint: Silence that ends your sentence. Raise it if pauses split your sentences.

interphone.title: Interphone Transmit
interphone.hint: Crew calls follow the captain's audio panel

acpGating.label: ACP transmit gating
acpGating.hint: Calls to ground or cabin need INT or CAB selected on the audio panel.
acpGating.more: Moving the selector away mid-call hangs up. Off, or an older ProSim: calls are always accepted.

intRequired.label: Require the INT key pressed
intRequired.hint: Ground calls also need the INT key held while you speak.
intRequired.more: Leave off unless your panel has the key.

sterile.title: Sterile Cockpit
sterile.hint: A quiet cockpit during the busy phases
sterile.enabledHint: The FO holds non-essential speech below the ceiling.

ceiling.label: Ceiling
ceiling.hint: Sterile below this altitude in climb, descent and approach.
ceiling.more: Cruise and ground are never sterile.

dropLow.label: Drop Low-priority speech
dropLow.hint: Advisories are dropped while sterile, never replayed.

normalPolicy.label: Normal-priority policy
normalPolicy.hint: What happens to normal speech while sterile.
normalPolicy.more: Allow is the safe default. Checklists and briefings are normal priority and are needed on a low approach.

exemptCabin.label: Exempt cabin reports
exemptCabin.hint: Cabin reports still come through while sterile.

fo.title: First Officer Voice
fo.hint: One list over every connected provider, grouped by provider and region. Nothing is pre-filled: only what each service reports

picker.label: First Officer
picker.hint: The provider it names speaks first. The others cover when it is down.
picker.more: Pick from any connected provider. Each provider also keeps a fallback voice on its own tab under Voice Providers, used when it covers for the one named here. Empty keeps the old behaviour: every provider speaks with its own fallback voice.

lists.label: Voice lists
lists.hint: Read from each connected provider when the page opens.

crew.title: Crew Voices
crew.hint: Who speaks for the cabin, the company and the ground crew. Blank is the First Officer's voice

purser.label: Purser voice
purser.hint: Cabin reports on the cabin interphone.

company.label: Company voice
company.hint: Dispatch messages, read out like ACARS.

companyFilter.label: Company intercom filter
companyFilter.hint: Off by default. A company message is a printout, not a phone call.

ground.label: Ground crew voice
ground.hint: Ground crew replies and calls on the interphone.

accents.title: Accent Localization
accents.hint: The ground crew's accent follows the airport's country

enabled.hint: Ground crew only. Purser and company keep the voices above.
enabled.more: Needs the Google provider for most accents. Local only mode falls back to US or UK.

persona.label: Chirp 3 HD persona
persona.hint: Google voice persona, for example Charon.

accents.overridesAfter: in config/settings.json (airport code prefix to voice locale).

groundCrew.title: Ground Crew
groundCrew.hint: Hail the ground crew and hear their calls

requireInt.label: Require INT selected
requireInt.hint: Ground speech waits until INT is selected on an audio panel.

intGrace.label: INT grace
intGrace.hint: After this wait the call plays anyway.

mechCall.label: MECH call on upcalls
mechCall.hint: Flash the MECH light when the ground crew calls you.

hailWindow.label: Hail listen window
hailWindow.hint: How long the crew waits for your request after answering.

upcalls.title: Upcalls
upcalls.hint: Each call comes once per turnaround

wording.title: Ground Crew Wording
wording.hint: Spoken word for word. {fuel} becomes the tonnes on board

cabin.title: Cabin Crew
cabin.hint: Purser reports on the cabin interphone

secure.label: Cabin secure report
secure.hint: Before takeoff, once the doors are closed and the beacon is on.

secureMinWait.label: Cabin secure: minimum wait
secureMinWait.hint: The crew needs this long after doors closed + beacon on before the report. 0 = instant.

securePerPax.label: Cabin secure: extra per passenger
securePerPax.hint: A random share of pax × this is added, drawn once per flight — sometimes ready after pushback, sometimes at the runway.
securePerPax.more: Passengers = GSX's boarded count, else the OFP figure. With 45 s and 1 s/pax a full A320 waits between 45 s and about 4 minutes. 0 = the minimum only.

ready.label: Cabin ready report
ready.hint: On approach, below the altitude set here.

requireCab.label: Require CAB selected
requireCab.hint: The purser waits until CAB is selected on an audio panel, or the grace time.

autoGround.label: FO answers cabin calls on the ground
autoGround.hint: During pushback, engine start and taxi-out the FO selects CAB on the FO's audio panel after the delay, so the report plays without you touching the ACP.
autoGround.more: This is the one place the cabin crew writes to the aircraft: the FO panel's CAB reception latch (S_ASP2_CAB_REC_LATCH; the captain's panel when you fly from the right seat), set on and released after the report. Never while the FO is mid-dialogue with you, never in any other phase. Off by default.

autoAir.label: FO answers cabin calls in the air
autoAir.hint: In descent and approach the FO answers the cabin-ready call after the delay.

dingStartup.label: Ding on startup
dingStartup.hint: Cabin chime when the app starts.

dingFinal.label: Ding on final loadsheet
dingFinal.hint: Cabin chime when the final loadsheet is sent.

ambient.label: Ambient events
ambient.hint: Now and then the purser reports a boarding delay.

cruiseQuery.label: Purser cruise query
cruiseQuery.hint: Once per flight in the cruise the purser calls: 'Flight deck, cabin. Any update on arrival time or turbulence for the service?' — then listens for your answer.
cruiseQuery.more: Chime and CAB channel as for every report. Answer in your own words: a time ('about forty minutes', 'on time', 'ten minutes late') or the ride ('smooth', 'light chop', 'expect some bumps') gets a matching acknowledgement, anything else 'copied, thank you', silence 'we'll check back later'. The reply is only ever acknowledged — never read as a command. A free answer needs the LAN speech server; the offline Windows engine hears a short list of likely replies. The call waits while the FO's ear is paused or another dialogue has the mic, and is skipped if the descent begins first.

cruiseQueryAfter.label: Cruise query after
cruiseQueryAfter.hint: Minutes into the cruise before the purser calls, give or take thirty percent.

cruiseQueryWindow.label: Cruise query reply window
cruiseQueryWindow.hint: How long the purser listens for your answer.

turbulence.title: Turbulence
turbulence.hint: The ride from the vertical acceleration, and what the cabin does about it

detect.label: Detect turbulence
detect.hint: Judge the ride (none / light / moderate / severe) from the aircraft's vertical acceleration.
detect.more: The unit of the raw value is learned while parked: about 1 means G, 9.8 means m/s², 32 means ft/s². A chip in the Flight Status hero shows the level. Off by default.

unit.label: Acceleration unit
unit.hint: Auto learns it from the at-rest reading. Force a unit only if the chip is clearly wrong.

light.label: Light from
light.hint: Deviation from the baseline over two seconds, in g. Placeholders until confirmed in the sim.

seatbeltAdvice.label: Seat-belt advice
seatbeltAdvice.hint: At light turbulence or worse with the sign off, the FO asks "seat belt signs, captain?" once per episode.

purserCall.label: Purser call in turbulence
purserCall.hint: At moderate the purser calls and asks whether to secure the cabin; at severe the crew seats itself and says so.
purserCall.more: Say yes and the crew is seated; the cabin reports secured 30–90 seconds later. Two minutes after the ride settles the purser reports the cabin back to normal.

pa.title: Captain's PA
pa.hint: Prompts for your own announcements, and the purser's PAs

prompts.label: "Captain, your PA" prompts
prompts.hint: The FO prompts your PA after take-off, at the top-of-descent notice, and when the seat-belt sign goes on in cruise turbulence.
prompts.more: A PA script card appears on Flight Status with the live facts filled in. You read it over the cabin PA — nothing speaks it for you.

purserAudible.label: Purser PAs audible
purserAudible.hint: Hear the purser's cabin PAs over the cabin filter: arm doors on beacon on, doors to manual with the engines off, prepare the cabin at 10,000 ft.

wording.title: Cabin Wording

securingReply.label: Hail reply while securing
securingReply.hint: Answer to a hail while the cabin-secure wait is still running.

wording.cruiseQueryHint: The purser's question in the cruise.

eta.label: Cruise query — time reply
eta.hint: After an answer naming a time or the arrival.

ride.label: Cruise query — ride reply
ride.hint: After an answer about turbulence or a smooth ride.

noReply.label: Cruise query — no reply
noReply.hint: When the window closes in silence.

company.title: Company Channel
company.hint: Dispatch messages read out like ACARS: the loadsheet, and now and then a cruise message

autoLoadsheet.label: Read the loadsheet automatically
autoLoadsheet.hint: Before departure, as soon as the final loadsheet is in. Off: only on "request loadsheet" or the web button.

chime.label: ACARS chime before messages
chime.hint: The double beep before a company delivery.

cruiseMessages.label: Cruise messages
cruiseMessages.hint: A short company message in the cruise, some flights.
cruiseMessages.more: Deterministic template around the destination facts. Off by default.

cruiseProb.label: Cruise message probability
cruiseProb.hint: 0.15 is about one flight in seven, drawn once per flight.

movementMessages.label: Movement messages
movementMessages.hint: An ACARS MVT message to the cockpit at take-off (AD with the ETA) and on blocks (AA).
movementMessages.more: Sent to the RCVD MSGS list in slots 06 and 07, beside the loadsheets. Needs ProSim and a loaded OFP. Off by default.

movementMessagesSpoken.label: Read the movement message aloud
movementMessagesSpoken.hint: The FO says "movement message sent" after each uplink.

delayCodes.label: Delay codes
delayCodes.hint: When you leave the gate later than the schedule plus the tolerance, the FO asks for the IATA delay code.
delayCodes.more: Answer with the number ("delay code one five") or the reason ("delay boarding"). No answer in five minutes files 99, other. The code goes into the movement message, the debrief and the logbook.

delayTolerance.label: On-time tolerance
delayTolerance.hint: Minutes after the scheduled departure that still count as on time. Airlines use 15.

company.delayCodesFile: The code list is delay-codes.json in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ProsimCompanion\config — add your airline's codes and the words you say for them.

persist.label: Save the spoken loadsheet
persist.hint: Written beside the session log as *.loadsheet.txt, with the raw EFB loadsheet.

debrief.title: Post-flight Debrief
debrief.hint: Spoken at shutdown from what the session recorded

length.label: Length
length.hint: Brief leaves out the activity counts and the fuel-used lines.

style.label: Style with the language model
style.hint: Warmer wording, every number verified. Off: the plain template.
style.more: Uses the model configured on Briefings & LLM. With that model off this has no effect.

day.title: Company Day
day.hint: Multi-sector duty tracking: block and duty figures, turnaround summaries, an end-of-day round-up. Not a flight-time-limits calculation

track.label: Track duty days automatically
track.hint: Off: "start duty day" and the /day page still work by hand.

turnaround.label: Speak the turnaround summary
turnaround.hint: At on-blocks: block time, schedule delta, open tech-log items.

allowance.label: Post-flight allowance
allowance.hint: Minutes added after the last on-blocks for the duty figure.

fdpWarning.label: FDP warning
fdpWarning.hint: A line on the Day page and one spoken line at the turnaround when the next sector would run past the EASA basic maximum for your report time and sector count.
fdpWarning.more: Advisory only: acclimatisation, extensions, split duty and rest rules are not modelled. The table is config/ftl-easa.json.

reportBefore.label: Report before first session
reportBefore.hint: Minutes before the day's first session the report time is assumed, when the rotation file has none.

day.fdpFileHint: The FDP maximum table is ftl-easa.json in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ProsimCompanion\config — edit it for your operator's scheme.

autoClose.label: Auto-close after idle
autoClose.hint: Close an open day after this long idle in a turnaround. 0 = never.

rotations.label: Planned rotations folder
rotations.hint: One JSON file per planned day. The README.txt in the folder shows the format. Empty uses the folder shown.

techLog.title: Tech Log & MEL
techLog.hint: The paperwork layer: deferral categories, due dates, preflight briefs. Never a failure, never a dataref write

offer.label: Offer tech-log entries after an abnormal
offer.hint: After shutdown the FO offers to log each abnormal handled this flight. Silent on a normal flight.

wear.label: Random wear
wear.hint: A small chance per flight of a benign cabin defect appearing at shutdown, from the wear pool.

rectify.label: Rectify on the due date
rectify.hint: Close open defects by itself when their MEL due date passes.
rectify.more: Off by default: rectification is meant to be your maintenance action.

openItems.label: Open items in the briefings
openItems.hint: The departure briefing names the open items; the arrival briefing only those that affect the landing.
openItems.more: Three titles at most, then 'and N more'. Landing-relevant = MEL category A or B, or an item about brakes, gear, spoilers, reversers, autobrake or anti-skid. Titles are spoken as written.

flagLines.label: Flag checklist lines
flagLines.hint: A spoken checklist line about a system with an open item gets 'note, open tech log item: …' after the challenge.
flagLines.more: Lines carry a system tag in the checklist JSON (apu, gear, autobrake, anti-ice, …); the shipped checklists tag the obvious ones. An item's System field on the Tech Log page, or a word of its title, is what the tag matches. Once per item per checklist run.

wearPool.label: Wear-pool file
wearPool.hint: Empty uses the shipped pool beside the exe.

techLog.raiseBefore: Raise and rectify defects on the
techLog.raiseAfter: page, or by voice ("raise a defect", "log a snag").

logbook.title: Pilot Logbook
logbook.hint: Every completed flight folded in at shutdown; totals are computed when shown
logbook.flightsBefore: The flights, the touchdown trend and the CSV export are on the

sayIntentions.title: SayIntentions
sayIntentions.hint: Online ATC: radio requests, weather, CPDLC and the arrival gate

use.label: Use SayIntentions
use.more: Voice requests need SayIntentions running with an active flight. Weather only needs the API key.

sayIntentions.apiKeySourceHint: Auto reads the key from SayIntentions' flight.json.

manualKey.label: Manual API key
manualKey.hint: Used only with Manual. Never logged.

ptt.label: Push-to-talk from the cockpit
ptt.hint: A ProSim PTT switch keys SayIntentions. Bind your sidestick or hand-mic button to that switch in ProSim first.
ptt.more: On each press the app sets the SayIntentions control LVAR to 1, on release to 0, through SimConnect — the client's 'Map PTT inside the sim with an LVAR'. No joystick polling. Needs MSFS running. The session log shows each press and whether SayIntentions transmitted.

pttControl.label: SayIntentions PTT control
pttControl.hint: Which SayIntentions radio or intercom the button keys. COM radio PTT is the one almost everybody needs.

foSpeaks.label: FO speaks the transmission
foSpeaks.hint: The FO says the radio call out loud before it is sent.
foSpeaks.more: Turn off if SayIntentions plays it as well (double audio).

autoTune.label: Auto-tune frequency
autoTune.hint: Tune the matched station before transmitting.

departureGate.label: Departure comms gate (legacy)
departureGate.hint: Legacy: comms come back to you near the runway, using SayIntentions' own distance figure.
departureGate.more: Ignored while the Comms hand-over card below is on — that flow uses the app's runway data and the flight phase, which the legacy gate lacked on the 2026-10-10 flight (it never tripped).

gateDistance.label: Gate distance (legacy)
gateDistance.hint: Distance from the runway where the legacy gate hands comms back to you.

wrongFreq.label: Wrong-frequency report
wrongFreq.hint: The FO tells you when COM1 is not on the frequency ATC gave you.
wrongFreq.more: It uses ATC's last 'Contact … on …' instruction and says it once. It is quiet at the gate, and when it cannot read the instruction.

waitBefore.label: Wait before the report
waitBefore.hint: How long COM1 may stay on another frequency first.

arrivalGate.label: Arrival gate from ATC
arrivalGate.hint: Use the gate SayIntentions ATC assigns as the GSX arrival gate.
arrivalGate.more: Only a gate that differs from the departure stand and appears from the climb onward counts. A gate you set yourself on the OFP page always wins. After landing the gate goes to GSX straight away. Off by default: the ATC pick may not exist in the loaded scenery.

handover.title: Comms hand-over
handover.hint: Who works the radios in each phase: you or the SayIntentions copilot

enabled.label: Hand the radios over by flight phase
enabled.hint: The copilot has them at the gate, on the taxi and in the cruise; you take them at the holding point and on the approach.
enabled.more: Each hand-over is one FO line and a session event. Say 'I have the radios' or 'you have the radios' to override at any time. Turning this on makes the legacy departure comms gate above irrelevant.

gate.label: Gate: copilot takes the radios
gate.hint: When SayIntentions starts a flight on the ground the copilot handles clearance, push and start.

taxi.label: FO reads the taxi clearance
taxi.hint: While the copilot has the radios, the FO reads ATC's taxi instruction out to you.
taxi.more: From SayIntentions' comms history, checked every 20 seconds — the line can lag the exchange by that much.

handoffs.label: FO announces hand-offs
handoffs.hint: While the copilot has the radios, the FO tells you each 'Contact … on …' ATC gives, on the ground and in the air.

holding.label: Holding point: you take the radios
holding.hint: Taxiing out, close to the departure runway, the radios become yours for the takeoff request and clearance.
holding.more: The runway comes from the FMS (else SayIntentions' plan) and its threshold from ProSim's runway list or the Navigraph data. Without a known runway this step cannot fire.

holdingDistance.label: Holding point distance
holdingDistance.hint: How close to the runway threshold counts as the holding point.

tuneTower.label: Tune Tower at the holding point
tuneTower.hint: COM1 goes to Tower when you take the radios there, if a Tower frequency is known.
tuneTower.more: ATC's last 'Contact Tower on …' first, else the airport's frequency list. Through SayIntentions, never a cockpit switch.

climb.label: Climb: copilot takes the radios back
climb.hint: After the takeoff clearance and the first departure hand-off, at the climb.

approach.label: Approach: you take the radios
approach.hint: For the landing clearance — at the approach, or as soon as ATC hands you to Tower in the descent.

taxiIn.label: Taxi in: copilot takes the radios back
taxiIn.hint: Once you are off the runway.

voiceOverride.label: Voice override
voiceOverride.hint: 'I have the radios' / 'you have the radios' flips who has them, at any time.

holdingLine.label: FO line at the holding point
holdingLine.hint: Spoken when you take the radios at the holding point.

approachLine.label: FO line on the approach
approachLine.hint: Spoken when you take the radios for the landing.

copilotLine.label: FO line when the copilot takes the radios
copilotLine.hint: Spoken at the gate, in the climb and on the taxi in.

captainLine.label: FO line when you take the radios by voice

weather.title: SayIntentions Weather
weather.hint: ATIS, METAR, TAF and CPDLC. Needs only the API key

cacheTtl.label: Cache TTL
cacheTtl.hint: How long a weather report is kept.

kokoro.title: Kokoro (local neural TTS)
kokoro.hint: Free neural voices from a Kokoro server on this PC or your network. Tried first

baseUrl.hint: Server address, for example http://192.168.1.50:8880. Empty turns Kokoro off.

fallback.hint: Used when Kokoro covers for the provider the First Officer or a crew voice names. Pick the main voices on the Voices page.
fallback.more: The grade is Kokoro's estimate of how much and how clean the training audio was, A down to F. British and American voices make a usable First Officer; the other languages read English badly.
fallback.empty: No voice list yet. Enter the server address and press Refresh voices.

kokoro.listHint: Read from the server when the page opens. Refresh after you add a blended voice.

connectTimeout.label: Connect timeout
connectTimeout.hint: Wait for the server to answer.
connectTimeout.more: Kept short on purpose. A sleeping server falls through to the next voice instead of stalling a callout.

bodyTimeout.label: Body timeout
bodyTimeout.hint: Time allowed for the audio to arrive.
bodyTimeout.more: Plus 100 ms per character, so a long briefing never trips the 60 s cooldown.

elevenLabs.title: ElevenLabs
elevenLabs.hint: Paid cloud neural voices with your own key. Cached, with a monthly budget. Tried after Kokoro and before Google

apiKey.hint: From elevenlabs.io, your profile, API keys. Empty turns ElevenLabs off. Never logged.
apiKey.more: The Free plan works for testing but has no commercial licence. Starter and up are licensed.

fallback.hint: Used when ElevenLabs covers for the provider the First Officer or a crew voice names. Pick the main voices on the Voices page.
fallback.more: ElevenLabs needs a voice here to count as configured; picking an ElevenLabs voice for the First Officer fills it for you.
fallback.empty: No voice list yet. Enter the key and press Refresh voices.

elevenLabs.listHint: The ElevenLabs premade voices, read with the key above.
elevenLabs.modelHint: Flash is fast and costs half. v3 is the most expressive, slower and full price.

format.label: Output format
format.hint: MP3 works on every plan and is decoded on this PC. PCM needs a paid plan and skips the decode.

stability.label: Stability
stability.hint: 0 to 1. Higher is steadier and less expressive.

similarity.label: Similarity
similarity.hint: 0 to 1. How closely the output follows the original voice.

speed.label: Speed
speed.hint: 0.7 to 1.2. 1.0 is the voice's natural pace.

budget.hint: ElevenLabs stops for the month at this many characters. 0 is no limit.
budget.more: Plan credits per month: Free 10,000, Starter 30,000, Creator 121,000. Flash costs about half a credit per character. The next voice in the chain takes over.

maxChars.label: Max characters per request
maxChars.hint: Longer texts skip ElevenLabs and use the next voice. 0 is no limit.
maxChars.more: The Free plan caps one generation at about 2,500 characters.

normalisation.label: Text normalisation
normalisation.hint: Let ElevenLabs expand numbers and abbreviations itself.
normalisation.more: Off is right for the FO: the app already writes numbers the spoken way, and the ElevenLabs normaliser mangles aviation words.

baseUrl.hint: Only change this for a proxy or a regional endpoint.

elevenLabs.timeoutHint: Whole request. The next voice takes over when it runs out.

google.title: Google Cloud TTS (Chirp 3 HD)
google.hint: Paid neural voices. Cached, with a monthly budget. Tried after ElevenLabs

keyFile.label: Service-account key file
keyFile.hint: Path to the service-account JSON key. Empty turns Google off. Never logged.

fallback.hint: Used when Google covers for the provider the First Officer or a crew voice names. Pick the main voices on the Voices page.
fallback.more: Google needs a voice here to count as configured; picking a Google voice for the First Officer fills it for you. The accent localization persona (Voices page) is a Google voice too.
fallback.empty: No voice list yet. Enter the key file path and press Refresh voices.

google.listHint: Google's Chirp 3 HD voices, read with the key file above.

budget.hint: Google stops for the month at this many characters. 0 is no limit.
budget.more: The free tier is 1,000,000 characters. The offline voices take over.

windows.title: Windows Voices
windows.hint: Offline voices on this PC, always available. The last two in the chain

sapi.label: SAPI5 fallback voice
sapi.hint: Last-resort voice. Empty uses the Windows default.

windows.listHint: The voices installed on this PC.

folder.label: TTS cache folder
folder.more: One folder per provider and voice. The usage counter lives there too.

mcdu.title: MCDU
mcdu.hint: Voice MCDU: reading always works, key presses need arming
mcdu.enabledHint: Read the MCDU, tune the ILS and change the arrival runway by voice.

actuation.label: Allow actuation
actuation.hint: Let the FO press MCDU keys.
actuation.more: Off: read only. Commands answer that key presses are off.

verifyPause.label: Verify pause
verifyPause.hint: The FO announces the change, then waits this long so you can cancel.

foSide.title: FO-side duties
foSide.hint: The FO sets its own altimeter and ND and cross-checks the ADIRS and the FMGC — nothing on your side

baroFollow.label: Baro follow
baroFollow.hint: The FO follows your altimeter: STD when yours goes to STD, your QNH when it comes back or changes. Also "QNH one zero one three" and "your side standard" by voice.
baroFollow.more: Every change is announced, waits three seconds for "negative", is written to the FO side only and read back. If the FO side is in inches the FO says so and leaves it.

efisCommands.label: EFIS commands
efisCommands.hint: "Your range forty", "ND to arc": the FO's own ND range and mode. Say "your" or "ND" so your own words are never taken.

adirsCheck.label: ADIRS / FMGC cross-check
adirsCheck.hint: "Cross-check": ADIRS alignment, the INIT page against the plan, the PERF speeds against the computed figures. Runs once by itself when the FMGC init settles at the gate.
adirsCheck.more: Read-only — no MCDU key is pressed. Cost index has no dataref and is read from the plan.

foSide.fileCommandsHint: The bare "set standard" and "set QNH" are file commands (commands.json) and stay there.

briefing.title: Briefings
briefing.hint: Departure and arrival briefings from nav data and weather

source.label: Procedure source
source.hint: Where the runway, SID, STAR and approach come from.
source.more: Auto tries the FMS plan, then SayIntentions, then the manual entries below, field by field.

verify.label: Verify numbers in LLM output
verify.hint: Every figure the LLM writes is checked against the facts.
verify.more: A failed check falls back to the plain template.

briefing.dfdBefore: The Navigraph DFD database path lives under

manual.title: Manual Procedure Overrides
manual.hint: Used when the FMS or SayIntentions cannot fill a field, or always in Manual mode

approach.label: Approach
approach.hint: For example I16R. Empty picks the best published approach, ILS first.
approach.more: Ask the FO "which approach" to hear the candidates.

minima.title: Minima Capture
minima.hint: The FO asks for the minimums during the arrival brief

interactive.label: Interactive capture
interactive.hint: The FO asks, reads back, and arms the minimums callouts.
interactive.more: A value already set on the Status section skips the question. Works best with a transcription server.

listenTimeout.label: Listen timeout
listenTimeout.hint: How long the FO waits for your answer.

maxRetries.label: Max retries
maxRetries.hint: Failed tries before the brief goes on as not briefed.

missed.title: Missed-Approach Re-brief
missed.hint: After a go-around the FO reads the missed approach

enabled.hint: Waits for the delay and gear up, so you fly first.
enabled.more: Without published legs the FO gives a prompt instead.

hardCeiling.label: Hard ceiling
hardCeiling.hint: Speaks by this time even if the gear never comes up.

emergency.title: Emergency Briefing & Threats
emergency.hint: The emergency half of the takeoff briefing and the go-around half of the arrival briefing

takeoff.label: Takeoff emergency brief
takeoff.hint: After the standard clauses the FO briefs the rejected-takeoff split, engine failure after V1, the acceleration altitude, the MSA, the return and the threats of the day.
takeoff.more: Off keeps the departure briefing exactly as before. Needs the Navigraph DFD for the MSA and a published engine-out SID; without it the FO briefs straight ahead on runway heading.

askForThreats.label: Ask for other threats
askForThreats.hint: The FO ends with "any other threats, captain?" and notes your answer.
askForThreats.more: Free text needs the transcription server. With the offline engine the question times out to "no further threats".

arrival.label: Arrival go-around brief
arrival.hint: Adds the missed-approach altitude, the MSA and the go-around split to the arrival briefing.

accelAlt.label: Acceleration altitude
accelAlt.hint: Above the airport. The FO adds the airport elevation when the DFD knows it.

emergency.sources: The runway surface and the icing threat come from the METAR, the MSA and the engine-out routing from the Navigraph DFD, FLEX/TOGA from the FMS or the last Takeoff calculation.

llm.title: LLM Styling
llm.hint: One language model for the briefing and debrief prose
llm.enabledHint: Off: plain templates only. Nothing leaves this PC.

stream.label: Speak while the model writes
stream.hint: The FO starts speaking after the first sentence, not after the whole reply. Each sentence is checked before it is spoken.
stream.more: If a sentence has a wrong number, or the model stops, the plain template finishes the briefing. Nothing starts again from the top. Off: the FO waits for the whole reply (the old behaviour).

apiFlavour.label: API flavour
apiFlavour.hint: Pick Ollama when the address is an Ollama server.
apiFlavour.more: Only the Ollama type can switch model thinking off.

baseUrl.hint: OpenAI style: the API root, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1. Ollama: the server root, e.g. http://localhost:11434.

llm.apiKeyHint: Never logged. Empty for local servers without a key.
llm.modelHint: Model name, e.g. gpt-4o-mini or qwen3.6:27b. Empty turns styling off.

thinking.label: Enable model thinking (slower, deeper reasoning)
thinking.hint: Lets a thinking model reason first. Slow: often 10 s or more.
thinking.more: Ollama only. Leave off for briefings.

llm.timeoutHint: Per call. A styled briefing may make two calls.
llm.testBefore: Save, then press "Test LLM connection" on the

ask.title: Ask the First Officer
ask.hint: Free-form questions, answered by the language model from live facts. Spoken only — never acted on

enabled.hint: Ask in plain words: 'what is our fuel on board', 'how long to top of descent', 'tell me the destination weather'. The FO answers from what the app knows right now.
enabled.more: Needs the LLM above and the LAN speech recognition server (the offline Windows engine only hears exact phrases). Every number in the answer is checked against the live facts; an unverifiable answer becomes 'I don't have a verified answer for that'. A question is tried only after every exact phrase has been ruled out, so nothing you could say before changes. In the sterile cockpit (below the sterile ceiling in climb, descent and approach) a question is heard but not answered.

smallTalk.label: Small talk and fun facts
smallTalk.hint: Ask anything: 'who is better, Chelsea or Arsenal', 'tell me a fun fact', 'what is the capital of Peru'. The FO answers from general knowledge, in character, one or two light sentences.
smallTalk.more: A question that mentions the flight (fuel, weights, speeds, altitude, runway, weather, times, passengers…) still takes the strict path: fact sheet only, every number verified. On the small-talk path numbers are not verified — they are trivia — but a sentence about this flight with a figure in it is refused and the FO says 'I don't have a verified answer for that'. With this on, no lead-in word is needed: any sentence of four words or more that matched nothing else and is shaped like a question (a question word up front, or the recognizer's question mark) goes to the FO; a plain remark is not sent. Still speech only, still silent in the sterile cockpit.

roger.label: Answer acknowledgements with 'Roger'
roger.hint: 'No questions, thank you for the briefing', 'copied', 'okay thanks': on, the FO says 'Roger.'; off, nothing at all.
roger.more: Either way such words never go to the language model and never earn a 'didn't catch that'. With small talk on, only something shaped like a question (a question word up front, or a question mark from the recognizer) is sent to the model.

flyingOver.label: 'What are we flying over?'
flyingOver.hint: Ask 'what are we flying over', 'where are we', 'what is that city on the left'. The FO names the country, the mountains or sea, and the nearest towns with distance and side — at once, from an atlas in the app — then adds a fact or two about them.
flyingOver.more: The position line comes from a built-in offline atlas (Natural Earth outlines, GeoNames towns — see the manual for the attribution), never from the language model, so it needs no internet and is always the same for the same spot. The facts after it come from the LLM: with 'Wikipedia facts' off, from its own knowledge, like small talk (numbers unverified, nothing about this flight). No lead-in word or minimum length is needed for these phrases. Works with small talk off.

wikipedia.label: Wikipedia facts
wikipedia.hint: With the switch above: fetch a short Wikipedia summary of the nearest town and have the FO take its facts from that instead of the model's memory.
wikipedia.more: One small request to en.wikipedia.org per place, three-second limit, answered from a cache after the first time. If it fails or finds nothing, the FO still gives the position and falls back to the model's own knowledge. Nothing about you or the flight is sent — only the place name.

leadIns.label: Question lead-ins
leadIns.hint: Comma-separated. An utterance must start with one of these to count as a question (not needed with small talk on).

minWords.label: Minimum words
minWords.hint: Shorter utterances are never questions — they are exact phrases, misheard.

timeBudget.label: Time budget
timeBudget.hint: From the question to the first spoken word. After this the FO gives up with the fixed line.

standBy.label: 'Stand by' after
standBy.hint: Silence before the FO says 'Stand by'. 0 = never.

regionFacts.title: Region Facts
regionFacts.hint: In the cruise the FO now and then offers a short fact about the country or sea below. Unprompted, spoken only

enabled.hint: Every fifteen to thirty minutes in the cruise (your interval), the FO mentions something about the region you are over: 'We're over the Netherlands — a quarter of what you see down there sits below sea level.' Never the same region twice in a flight.
enabled.more: The region comes from the same built-in atlas as 'what are we flying over?' (no internet needed). The fact comes from the language model when it is on and healthy (two sentences, the same guard as the place facts — nothing about this flight), otherwise from the curated file region-facts.json in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ProsimCompanion\config — edit it to add your own, keyed by country code (FR, GB) or 'sea:North Sea'. Silent outside the cruise, while the flight is not live, while the FO's ear is paused, in the sterile cockpit, after 'quiet please', and over places the atlas does not name. With the FO persona on, a curated fact is spoken in the persona's voice with every figure locked.

shortest.label: Shortest gap
shortest.hint: Minutes between facts, at least. The first fact comes this long (plus the random share) after the cruise begins.

longest.label: Longest gap
longest.hint: Each gap is drawn at random between the two, so it never feels like a timer.

perFlight.label: Facts per flight
perFlight.hint: At most. Resets with the cabin's once-per-flight reports (cold and dark, or a new preflight after shutdown).

llmFacts.label: Facts from the language model
llmFacts.hint: Ask the LLM above for the fact when it is configured and healthy; off, or with the model down, only the curated file speaks.
llmFacts.more: Model facts stream sentence by sentence like the place facts; a sentence about this flight with a figure in it is refused, and if the model says nothing within twenty seconds the curated file speaks instead. Numbers in a model fact are trivia and are not verified.

wol.title: Wake-on-LAN
wol.before: The PCs the app wakes at startup — the language-model box, the speech server, any other — are one list on
wol.after: . An old single-PC setting from this page is moved there the first time Setup opens.

callouts.title: Standard Callouts
callouts.hint: The FO's speed, altitude and rollout calls.

enabled.label: Callouts enabled
enabled.hint: Master switch for every standard callout.
enabled.more: Applies live. The individual callout texts, altitude callouts, the other flow-monitor reminders and the weather advisories are edited in the sop section of settings.json for now.

placards.title: Flap Placards
placards.hint: Maximum speed per flap lever position (VFE). The FO warns when you approach or exceed it, and checks your flap calls against it.
placards.leverHint: ProSim reports the lever in six steps: UP, 1, 1+F, 2, 3, FULL. Lever 1 gives 1+F on the ground and on take-off; the FO reads the step ProSim reports.

gear.title: Gear Limits
gear.hint: VLE is the limit with the gear down. VLO is the limit while the gear moves; the FO refuses a gear call above it.

vle.label: Gear extended (VLE)
vle.hint: The FO warns when you fly faster than this with the gear down. 0 turns the warning off.

vloDown.label: Gear extension (VLO down)
vloDown.hint: "Gear down" is refused above this speed. 0 turns the check off.

vloUp.label: Gear retraction (VLO up)
vloUp.hint: "Gear up" is refused above this speed. 0 turns the check off.

stillDown.label: Gear still down reminder
stillDown.hint: The FO says "gear still down" when you climb with the gear down.

upBy.label: Gear up by
upBy.hint: The reminder comes when you climb above this height with the gear down.

gates.title: Approach Gates
gates.hint: The heights where the FO checks that the approach is stable. Airlines differ — set your own SOP.

stable.label: Stable approach check
stable.hint: At each gate the FO checks speed, sink rate, gear and flaps, and calls an unstable approach.
stable.more: A gate is checked once, when you descend through its height on the radio altimeter. The highest gate is checked first. The speed band is measured from VLS.

height.label: Height
height.hint: Radio altitude of the gate. 0 switches the gate off.

minFlap.label: Minimum flap lever
minFlap.hint: The flap lever must be at this position or further.

announce.label: Say "stabilized" when the gate passes
announce.hint: Off: the FO speaks at this gate only when the approach is unstable.

gates.addTitle: Add a gate, for example a 1500 ft gate
gates.resetTitle: Two gates: 1000 ft (flap 2 or more) and 500 ft (flap 3 or more), gear down at both

thrust.label: Thrust must be spooled up
thrust.hint: Adds a thrust check to every gate: the average N1 must be at or above the figure below.

advisories.title: Placard Advisories
advisories.hint: What the FO says when a limit is close or exceeded

warnWithin.label: Warn within
warnWithin.hint: Speak the approaching call this close below the limit, while accelerating.

cooldown.label: Cooldown
cooldown.hint: Minimum time between two advisories of the same kind.

monitoring.title: In-flight monitoring
monitoring.hint: Four FO duties that are off until you turn them on. Each needs a live flight and only ever speaks.

fuelCheck.label: Fuel check
fuelCheck.hint: In the cruise the FO compares fuel on board with the SimBrief plan at your position and gives the estimated landing fuel. Also on 'fuel check'.
fuelCheck.more: Needs a SimBrief OFP with a navlog and the aircraft position. Without them: fuel on board minus fuel flow times the time to the ETA. A shortfall beyond the margin is spoken at High. Silent in sterile phases.

fuelEvery.label: Fuel check every
fuelEvery.hint: Minutes between automatic checks in the cruise; 0 = on request only

shortfall.label: Shortfall margin
shortfall.hint: This far below plan (or more) the check is spoken as a warning

onPlan.label: Counts as on plan within
onPlan.hint: Smaller differences are 'on plan' instead of a figure

grossError.label: Takeoff gross error check
grossError.hint: One line before takeoff: the aircraft's weights against the final loadsheet, and the FMS flaps, flex and V-speeds against the last takeoff performance calculation. Also on 'gross error check'.
grossError.more: Runs once per departure when the final loadsheet is out and the V-speeds are in the FMS. The FMS INIT weights cannot be read from ProSim, so the aircraft's own zero fuel weight and fuel on board stand in for them. The performance figures come from the Performance page's last calculation.

automatic.label: Automatic
automatic.hint: Off = only when you ask for it

destWx.label: Destination weather watch
destWx.hint: From the cruise on, the FO tells you when the destination's visibility or ceiling crosses your limit, when the ATIS letter changes, or when the wind turns into a tailwind on the planned landing runway.
destWx.more: Uses the weather cards' own refresh, no extra polling. The alternate's weather is added once the destination is below a limit. Each kind of change is spoken at most once in the quiet period.

windLimits.label: Wind limits
windLimits.hint: "Wind check" and "runway condition" by voice, and a wind-limit line in the departure and arrival briefings.
windLimits.more: The limits are on Display & Flight Data → Aircraft limits. The landing runway condition comes from the Landing page.

windLimitAdvisory.label: Approach wind advisory
windLimitAdvisory.hint: On the approach the FO says once when the destination wind puts the landing runway beyond a limit.

tailwind.label: Tailwind limit
tailwind.hint: A tailwind component above this on the planned landing runway is announced

readbacks.label: Read-backs
readbacks.hint: Say 'altimeter one zero one three', 'V speeds one four one, one four four, one four seven', 'runway two seven right' or 'minimums two one zero' and the FO checks it against the aircraft.
readbacks.more: The altimeter is checked against your baro setting, the V-speeds against the FMS PERF page, the runway against the FMS plan (departure before takeoff, arrival after), the minimums against the ones you briefed. The FO answers 'checked' or the value it reads.

stepClimb.label: Step-climb advice
stepClimb.hint: In the cruise, near a planned step from the navlog, the FO says "planned step to flight level … at {fix}, captain" once per step. "When is our next step?" works any time.
stepClimb.more: Steps come from the altitude per fix on your SimBrief navlog. With SayIntentions on, the FO adds "say request climb" and "request climb" asks for the planned level.

stepClimbLead.label: Step-climb advice lead
stepClimbLead.hint: How far before the step fix the advice comes, direct distance.

abnormals.title: ECAM Abnormals
abnormals.hint: The FO reads the E/WD and the system datarefs, announces a failure and works the procedure with you. It never moves a switch

detect.label: Detect and announce failures
detect.hint: Off: nothing is detected or announced. The memory drills can still be called by voice as rehearsals.

lineByLine.label: Work the ECAM line by line
lineByLine.hint: Each action line waits for your confirm; a line with a check is verified against the aircraft.
lineByLine.more: Say "standby", "say again", "skip", "fault remains", "unable" or "cancel ecam" at any line. Off: the FO announces the failure and leaves the ECAM to you.

answerWindow.label: Answer window per line
answerWindow.hint: How long the FO waits for your answer before asking again.

silentPrompts.label: Unanswered prompts before standby
silentPrompts.hint: After this many silent windows in a row the FO stops asking and stands by. 0 = ask forever.

mismatches.label: Verify mismatches tolerated
mismatches.hint: Discrepancies on a checked line before the FO offers continue or standby.

rto.label: Rejected takeoff
rto.hint: Say "stop" or "reject" on the roll, or pull both thrust levers to idle above 40 kt: the FO calls reverse green, decel, seventy knots and "aircraft stopped, park brake", then offers the open ECAM.
rto.more: Above 100 kt the FO reads "stop" back first. After lift-off the FO refuses: "we're flying, captain". GSX and the departure are left alone — a second attempt on the same turnaround works and is logged.

efato.label: Engine failure after V1
efato.hint: One engine's N2 collapses between V1 and 400 ft while the other stays at takeoff thrust: "engine failure", then rudder, rotate, V2, positive climb — gear up, and ECAM actions at 400 ft.
efato.more: The ENG 1 / ENG 2 FAIL procedure takes over at 400 ft. Rehearse it on the ground with "engine failure after V1". Needs failure detection on.

abnormals.filesBefore: The procedures themselves are JSON files under
abnormals.filesAfter: ; a file that fails to load is named in a banner. A running dialogue can be cancelled from the Status section.

seat.left: Left seat (FO operates the right side)
seat.right: Right seat (virtual pilot operates the left side)

capture.failed: Capture failed — see the Logs page.

scan.failed: Scan failed — see the Logs page.

voiceNotes.emptyHint: No voices listed yet. Connect a provider under Voice Providers and press Refresh.
